title: Pictographs and Bar Graphs
seo_title: Grade 2 Pictographs and Bar Graphs Worksheets (TEKS 2.10)
standard_text: 2.10A explain that the length of a bar in a bar graph or the number of pictures in a pictograph represents the number of data points for a given category; 2.10B organize a collection of data with up to four categories using pictographs and bar graphs with intervals of one or more; 2.10C write and solve one-step word problems involving addition or subtraction using data represented within pictographs and bar graphs with intervals of one; 2.10D draw conclusions and make predictions from information in a graph
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 graph worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.10: read pictographs, tally charts and bar graphs, compare data, make graphs and draw conclusions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Read the bar or count the pictures; check the key.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a pictograph, count the pictures. Check the key if one picture stands for more than 1.
  • In a bar graph, read the number at the top of each bar.
  • How many more or fewer: subtract. In all: add.
  • Use the graph to draw conclusions, like which choice is the most popular.

Examples

Example

Bar graph: Dogs 9, Cats 5

9 − 5

Answer: 4 more dogs

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting grid lines instead of reading the barRead the number where the bar ends.
Misreading the keyIf each picture is 2, multiply.
Adding when asked how many moreHow many more means subtract.

sets.title: Read picture graphs and tally charts

items.q: How many votes did Summer get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Summer row: 1. So the answer is 1 vote.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Crow row. There are 7. So the answer is 7 birds.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Apple row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 votes.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Balls row: 1, 2. So the answer is 2 toys.

items.q: How many students chose swimming?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Swim row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 students.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Noah row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 books.

items.q: How many students ride the bus to school?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Bus row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So the answer is 6 students.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Pretzels row. There are 7. So the answer is 7 students.

items.q: How many bees did the class see?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Bee row. There are 8. So the answer is 8 bugs.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Green row: 1, 2, 3, 4. So the answer is 4 votes.

items.q: Which row shows the most stickers?
items.e: Each square is 1, so the row with the most squares wins. Lily has 9. The others have 5, 7, 6.
Each heart is 1, so the row with the fewest hearts wins. Cat has 2. The others have 7, 9, 5.

items.q: Which row shows 6 days?
items.e: Look for a row with 6 circles. Count the circles in the Cloudy row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
Each star is 1, so the row with the most stars wins. Nora has 9. The others have 6, 8, 3.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest scoops?
items.e: Each square is 1, so the row with the fewest squares wins. Vanilla has 1. The others have 9, 5, 3.
Look for a row with 4 hearts. Count the hearts in the Pasta row: 1, 2, 3, 4.

items.q: How many students come by car to school?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Car row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

items.q: How many votes did Yellow get?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Yellow row has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more marks. 5 + 5 + 2 = 12.

items.q: How many stickers does Emma have?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Emma row has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more marks. 5 + 5 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Which row shows the most books?
items.e: Find the row with the most marks. The Ava row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13. The other rows are Noah 10, Zoe 5, Leo 3.

items.q: How many votes did Grape get?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Grape bar ends at the line for 5. So the answer is 5 votes.

items.q: How many shells did Sam find?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Sam bar ends at the line for 3. So the answer is 3 shells.

items.q: How many robins came to the feeder?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Robin bar ends at the line for 4. So the answer is 4 birds.

items.q: How many students chose pretzels?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Pretzels bar ends at the line between 10 and 12. That line is 11. So the answer is 11 students.

items.q: How many votes did Spring get?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Spring bar ends at the line for 7. So the answer is 7 votes.

items.q: How many stickers does Lily have?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Lily bar ends at the line between 10 and 12. That line is 11. So the answer is 11 stickers.

items.q: How many students chose baseball?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Baseball bar ends at the line for 7. So the answer is 7 students.

items.q: How many students have a dog?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Dog bar ends at the line between 2 and 4. That line is 3. So the answer is 3 students.

items.q: How many ladybugs did the class see?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Ladybug bar ends at the line between 10 and 12. That line is 11. So the answer is 11 bugs.

items.q: How many cars are in the bin?
items.e: Each grid line is 1 more. The Cars bar ends at the line for 8. So the answer is 8 toys.

items.q: How many mint scoops were sold?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Mint bar ends at the line between 2 and 4. That line is 3. So the answer is 3 scoops.

items.q: How many votes did Blue get?
items.e: The numbers count by 2s, so the line between two numbers is the number in the middle. The Blue bar ends at the line between 2 and 4. That line is 3. So the answer is 3 votes.

items.q: Which bar shows 5 students?
items.e: Find 5 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Car bar ends at the line for 5.

items.q: Which bar shows 2 days?
items.e: Find 2 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Cloudy bar ends at the line for 2.

items.q: Which bar shows 7 students?
items.e: Find 7 on the numbers. Follow that line across. The Tacos bar ends at the line for 7.

items.q: Which bar shows the most books?
items.e: The Ava bar is the longest bar. The Ava bar ends at the line for 6. It shows 6 books.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest students?
items.e: The Baseball bar is the shortest bar. The Baseball bar ends at the line between 2 and 4. That line is 3. It shows 3 students.

items.q: Which bar shows the most days?
items.e: The Sunny bar is the longest bar. The Sunny bar ends at the line for 8. It shows 8 days.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest toys?
items.e: The Cars bar is the shortest bar. The Cars bar ends at the line between 4 and 6. That line is 5. It shows 5 toys.

items.q: Which two bars show the same number?
items.e: The Ava bar and the Maya bar both end at the line for 3. They are the same length.

sets.title: In all, how many more, how many fewer

items.q: How many students chose soccer or tennis?
items.e: Read each bar. Soccer: 8. Tennis: 3. Put them together: 8 + 3 = 11 students.

items.q: How many more students come by car to school than ride a bike?
items.e: Read each bar. Car: 8. Bike: 6. Compare: 8 − 6 = 2. The answer is 2 more students.

items.q: How many fewer stickers does Kai have than Omar?
items.e: Read each bar. Omar: 8. Kai: 2. Compare: 8 − 2 = 6. The answer is 6 fewer stickers.
Count the pictures in each row. Zoe: 9. Leo: 6. Put them together: 9 + 6 = 15 books.

items.q: How many more votes did Purple get than Blue?
items.e: Read each bar. Purple: 7. Blue: 3. Compare: 7 − 3 = 4. The answer is 4 more votes.

items.q: How many fewer students have a bird than a dog?
items.e: Read each bar. Dog: 7. Bird: 1. Compare: 7 − 1 = 6. The answer is 6 fewer students.

items.q: How many students chose yogurt or grapes?
items.e: Read each bar. Yogurt: 9. Grapes: 5. Put them together: 9 + 5 = 14 students.
Count the pictures in each row. Pizza: 9. Salad: 6. Compare: 9 − 6 = 3. The answer is 3 more students.

items.q: How many fewer blocks than balls are in the bin?
items.e: Read each bar. Balls: 6. Blocks: 2. Compare: 6 − 2 = 4. The answer is 4 fewer toys.

items.q: How many mint and berry scoops were sold in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Mint: 2. Berry: 3. Put them together: 2 + 3 = 5 scoops.

items.q: How many more votes did Pear get than Grape?
items.e: Read each bar. Pear: 10. Grape: 3. Compare: 10 − 3 = 7. The answer is 7 more votes.
Count the pictures in each row. Sam: 4. Eli: 1. Compare: 4 − 1 = 3. The answer is 3 fewer shells.

items.q: How many more votes does Fall need to have as many as Summer?
items.e: Read each bar. Summer: 4. Fall: 1. Fall needs to get from 1 up to 4. 4 − 1 = 3, so Fall needs 3 more votes.

items.q: How many days are shown in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Sunny: 6. Cloudy: 1. Windy: 2. Rainy: 5. Add all four: 6 + 1 + 2 + 5 = 14 days. (There are 4 bars, but the answer is the number of days.)

items.q: How many more ants than beetles did the class see?
items.e: Read each bar. Ant: 9. Beetle: 1. Compare: 9 − 1 = 8. The answer is 8 more bugs.
Count the pictures in each row. Blue Jay: 9. Crow: 1. Compare: 9 − 1 = 8. The answer is 8 fewer birds.

items.q: How many students do not ride a bike to school?
items.e: Leave out Bike. Add the other three: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 students.

items.q: How many more students need to choose pizza to match tacos?
items.e: Read each bar. Tacos: 8. Pizza: 3. Pizza needs to get from 3 up to 8. 8 − 3 = 5, so Pizza needs 5 more students.

items.q: How many scoops were sold in all?
items.e: Read each bar. Mango: 2. Vanilla: 10. Berry: 8. Mint: 4. Add all four: 2 + 10 + 8 + 4 = 24 scoops. (There are 4 bars, but the answer is the number of scoops.)

items.q: How many votes were not for Blue?
items.e: Leave out Blue. Add the other three: 1 + 4 + 8 = 13 votes.

items.q: Josiah made this bar graph from the data: Zoe 4, Noah 9, Leo 2, Maya 5. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Noah bar ends at 10, but the data says 9. It is one line too high.

items.q: Noah made this bar graph from the data: Baseball 2, Swim 9, Soccer 7, Tennis 6. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Swim bar ends at 8, but the data says 9. It is one line too low.

items.q: Harper made this bar graph from the data: Mint 9, Mango 3, Vanilla 5, Berry 7. Which bar is wrong?
items.e: Check each bar against the data. The Mango bar ends at 4, but the data says 3. It is one line too high.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Bird 1, Dog 3, Fish 6, Cat 2.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph C matches: Bird 1, Dog 3, Fish 6, Cat 2. Graph A has Cat and Dog switched; B has Cat 1; D has Bird 2.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Pear 4, Grape 6, Peach 3.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph A matches: Pear 4, Grape 6, Peach 3. Graph B has Peach 4; C has Pear 3; D has Pear and Peach switched.

items.q: Which bar graph shows this data? Kai 3, Emma 2, Lily 4, Omar 5.
items.e: Check every bar. Only graph D matches: Kai 3, Emma 2, Lily 4, Omar 5. Graph A has Lily and Kai switched; B has Kai 2; C has Omar 6.

items.q: Later, 6 more students choose salad. How many students choose salad now?
items.e: The Salad bar ends at the line for 4. Add the 6 new ones: 4 + 6 = 10 students.

items.q: Later, 3 more students vote for Summer. How many votes does Summer have now?
items.e: The Summer bar ends at the line for 7. Add the 3 new ones: 7 + 3 = 10 votes.

items.q: Ava wants to read 15 books this week. How many more books does she need to read?
items.e: The Ava bar ends at the line for 4. Ava has 4 and wants 15. 15 − 4 = 11 more books.

items.q: Owen wants to find 15 shells. How many more shells does he need to find?
items.e: The Owen bar ends at the line for 2. Owen has 2 and wants 15. 15 − 2 = 13 more shells.

items.q: All 17 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Bike is missing. How many students ride a bike to school?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 3 + 5 + 2 = 10. All 17 students: 17 − 10 = 7 students.

items.q: All 19 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Yogurt is missing. How many students chose yogurt?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 7 + 4 + 3 = 14. All 19 students: 19 − 14 = 5 students.

items.q: All 23 students in the class are in this graph. The bar for Bird is missing. How many students have a bird?
items.e: Add the bars you can see: 7 + 6 + 2 = 15. All 23 students: 23 − 15 = 8 students.

items.q: How many more birds do the Robin and Blue Jay bars show together than the Crow bar?
items.e: Step 1: Robin + Blue Jay = 5 + 4 = 9. Step 2: compare with Crow (7): 9 − 7 = 2 more birds.

items.q: How many more shells do the Sam and Mia bars show together than the Eli bar?
items.e: Step 1: Sam + Mia = 4 + 7 = 11. Step 2: compare with Eli (9): 11 − 9 = 2 more shells.

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: All the bars are the same.
Bananas got 4 more votes than Peaches.
Peaches got 24 more votes than Bananas.
Peaches got 4 more votes than Bananas.
items.e: 14 − 10 = 4, so Peaches got 4 more votes than Bananas.
